parsed.explanation: Combined regime has no criminal trans-existence law or documented visitor entry ban, but outing via immigration/detention/facility conflict is material. Top courts require vulnerability assessment before placing detained trans foreigners, corrected documents, and protect private life; anti-discrimination law covers gender identity. Yet prison rules are unsettled, immigration police practice inconsistent, senior officials demean trans people, and survey harassment/assault experience is high, especially among trans and non-binary respondents, with rural/nighttime risk. City openness is commercial-report level. For adults and parent-child travellers, no age-specific traveller restriction is documented, but unresolved custody/care questions keep exposure elevated. Rating sits in Elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border refusal or scanner rule; however passport mismatch handling and visitor registration are open questions, and immigration records include a detained trans foreigner.
entry_documents.protection: No trans-specific entry ban documented; regional court ordered corrected certificates; asylum law includes gender identity and offers a partner interview option.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry appears administratively unrestrictive in the record, but any immigration detention can trigger the inconsistent detention-placement pathway.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Administrative courts clashed over immigration-police handling; a lower court gave sarcastic moral lectures to a detained trans man; placement safeguards are inconsistently applied.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Supreme administrative court requires vulnerability assessment before placement and rebuked moralising; courts sometimes correct document issues.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A stopped or detained visitor can move into custody placement where prison rules remain unsettled.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prisons are documented as unprepared and without clear rules for people in or after transition; binding regulation is contested, so placement and protective custody remain uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Supreme court and human-rights commissioner demand explicit transition needs; commercial guides rate two major cities as open for solo travellers.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custody/facility exposure becomes acute after detention or arrest; everyday city facilities are not documented to impose trans-specific restrictions.

care_services.exposure: No documented refusal of visitor emergency, continuity, or gender-related care; resident medical gatekeeping is not shown to reach travellers.
care_services.protection: Health ministry post-2025 legal-gender reform is resident-facing climate only; asylum SOGI accommodation signals inclusive administration.
care_services.interaction: If care is sought after a document mismatch, ward placement and staff discretion are open questions not answered by the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of state called trans people disgusting; minister and far-right rhetoric frame trans rights as deviance; official hostility persists after court reforms.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2009 anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in services; a bias-motivated amendment was approved but remains pending; courts have intervened.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level hostility may embolden street and frontline discrimination, while functioning courts partly mediate without removing enforcement gaps.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented rule denying facilities, care, entry, school services, or guardian assistance specifically because a trans minor is travelling.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a parent/guardian with a minor, unknowns follow general facility/care and outing questions rather than an identified age-specific visitor restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Survey reports high five-year harassment, insult, and assault experience, highest among trans and non-binary respondents; commercial guides place risk in rural and late-night settings.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime bodies record prosecutions and sentences; city venues, hostels, and advocacy channels are reported as supportive; no documented organised police targeting of visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outing in nightlife or transport may invite confrontation or ejection; official response is uneven and bias statistics understate prevalence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Criminal bias amendment is pending; prison regulation is unresolved; surgery/hormone reform may be administrative and reversible; recorded bias statistics are inadequate.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional and regional courts found rights violations, ordered document corrections, imposed detention vulnerability assessment, and independent bodies press reforms.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies can reverse individual harms, but inconsistent frontline practice and missing binding rules keep traveller exposure material.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.55-A, routine bureaucratic encounters can create questioning and hold-ups, and remedies exist but are uneven. It sits lower because there is no documented universal visitor registration/checkpoint database, and higher than 0.45 because top-court safeguards and anti-discrimination law are documented.

Below 0.65-A because detention placement is unresolved and frontline immigration/custody practice is inconsistent; unlike the anchor, senior political hostility and high harassment prevalence reduce safety despite functioning courts.

Materially above 0.45-D: no universal hotel reporting, shared security database, or repeated official interviews for visitors is documented; exposure mainly follows detention or facility conflict rather than everyday registration.

parsed.synthesis: Documented protections and harms interact across levels: formal equality and top-court rulings lower severity when a traveller can access a judge, ombuds, or city venue; but immigration detention, unprepared prisons, and unsettled facility rules raise severity after discovery. Political hostility raises baseline social/friction without amounting to organised targeting. Absence of a visitor-facing entry ban prevents severe criminal exposure, while persistent frontline inconsistency, high harassment prevalence, and unresolved custody placement prevent Reduced-Risk safety.
